_doc: Everything libviprs-specific about the generated benchmark page at /benchmarks/. The renderer (render-latest.mjs) holds no series id, no colour, no threshold and no editorial sentence of its own: it reads them from here. That split is the K2.3 contract rule, and it is why a second family or a third backend is a config edit rather than a renderer edit. The key names follow the schema libviprs-bench#76 published (tools/contract/config.schema.json at cd65c76) wherever the two overlap, so the frozen dashboard reads this file rather than a translation of it. Two things are page-only and sit outside that schema: `families`, because this page carries two families on one axis where the dashboard carries one, and the editorial blocks (metricLabel, scenarioLabel, notMeasured), because the schema has nowhere for prose.

contract._doc: The revision the generated-section contract came from: the GENERATED:<name>:BEGIN/END splice, the --check exit codes, and the class names the markup uses (.results-table, .num, .conf, .status-callout, .section-head, .absent). libviprs-bench#76 freezes the files themselves at tools/contract/upstream/; this page implements the same contract against libviprs.org's own palette, because causl's dashboard.css is written against causl brand tokens that do not exist on this site. tools/render-latest.test.mjs::every_class_the_renderer_emits_is_styled is the drift gate on that.

archive._doc: Where the archived documents live in the capture workspace. The page never reads them at render time; import writes history.json and the renderer reads that. The path is here so the provenance section can say where to go and look.

era._doc: Two runs belong to the same comparable era only when every axis agrees. Upstream breaks an era on the series set alone; libviprs adds the host fingerprint and the filesystem type, because a run on a different machine or a different filesystem is a different experiment and one line across the two invents a change that never happened.

confidence._doc: The trustworthy floor is minTicksPerSample x the measured timer tick, both read from the document rather than written here, so a host with a different clock moves the floor rather than the prose. covLowConfidence mirrors what the producer used; the page states the producer's value, not this one, and this is only the fallback for a document that carries none.

noise._doc: A delta smaller than the spread the run's own replicate pair measured for that very key is noise, not a pass and not a regression. A spread that was not measured is not a spread, so the page refuses to rule rather than falling back to the thresholds: the capture's median spread is 3.46% and one metric's is 53.3%, so a median used as a fallback gets the dangerous answer confidently.

gate.label: measured, not gated
gate._doc: Only the literal false counts. Nobody said and not gated are different facts, and if absent counted as ungated the page would go silent the day the field moves.

verdict._doc: A chip is only ever drawn on a gateable cell whose kind is not in noChipKinds. Direction is read off the sample, per metric: ten of the thirty metric keys are higher-is-better, and a dashboard that compares raw numbers calls those a regression when they get faster.

requires: the run's provenance is observed rather than attested
the cell reached its minimum repetitions
the cell's timer did not saturate
the cell's own confidence is high
gateability._doc: Every one of these has to hold. A cell that misses any of them is published in full, with its number, and never carries a verdict chip: it reads 'measured, not gated'. Hiding it would make an untested backend and an untrusted measurement look the same, and chipping it would make a number its own producer refuses to vouch for look like a result.

storage.label: One archive against a directory tree

suppressedMetrics.build.peak_rss_mb: the engines sweep reads a process-wide high-water mark, so all three engines report the same figure and none of them reports its own (libviprs-bench#74). The tracked working set below is per engine and is the column that carries the memory story.

defaults._doc: What the interactive layer starts with when it attaches. `libraries` and `scales` are the schema's names for the default filter; `families` is this page's addition, because the dashboard has no notion of more than one.

scenarioLabel.first_lookup: the first tile out of a freshly opened artefact
scenarioLabel.read_sequential: walk every tile in storage order
scenarioLabel.read_tileid_order: walk every tile in tile-id order
scenarioLabel.read_plan_order: walk the tiles a viewport plan asks for

notMeasured.title: HTTP, and object storage
notMeasured.body: Every read on this page is a local file read. PMTiles is designed to be range-requested off a static host or a bucket, which is where a single addressable archive pays for itself hardest, and none of that is measured here. The request counts in the full results are the closest thing on the page, and they are a count rather than a timing.

notMeasured.title: A cold page cache
notMeasured.body: Cold means a cold reader: a fresh process opening an artefact it has not opened. The kernel's page cache is whatever the preceding work left it, which is why the run records the page-cache state as warm-unknown rather than claiming to have dropped it. A genuinely cold cache is a different measurement and would need the host to cooperate.

notMeasured.title: macOS, Windows, or any filesystem but this one
notMeasured.body: One host, one filesystem, one architecture. The directory backend in particular is a measurement of how a specific filesystem handles tens of thousands of small files, and that is exactly the number that moves most between filesystems. The era rule above is what stops a run from a different machine being drawn on the same line as this one.

notMeasured.title: Other codecs
notMeasured.body: One encoder, at one setting, for every cell. Tile bytes drive both the output totals and the read work, so a different codec moves both, and nothing here says by how much.

notMeasured.title: The directory backend's request counts
notMeasured.body: PMTiles counts the requests a reader actually issues, because the reader is the thing being measured and it knows. The directory tree has no reader to count: its index work happens in the kernel, one path resolution at a time. So its request figures are declared by a model of what an HTTP client would have to ask for, they are labelled declared everywhere they appear, and they are not a measurement of anything that ran.

series._doc: The dashboard-side series block in the schema's shape, carrying the default family. A page with more than one family needs one of these per family, so each entry under `families` repeats this shape and the renderer reads the family's copy. This one is what a consumer that knows nothing about families gets.

samples._doc: The fields a sample carries onto a chart point. groupSections builds a fixed-shape point and that point is the only thing computeVerdict sees, so a verdict rule that reads a field not in this list reads undefined, which looks exactly like a rule that is switched off. gated and gateBlockers are in here because the no-chip rule below is driven off them.
